name: Joni Mitchell
hook: A Canadian singer-songwriter whose 1970 environmental anthem became, because she personally said yes, a Janet Jackson hit twenty-seven years later.

blurb.age7: Joni Mitchell writes and sings her own songs. One of her songs from 1970 was used, with her permission, in a Janet Jackson song almost thirty years later.
blurb.age13: Joni Mitchell, born in Alberta, Canada, became one of the most admired singer-songwriters of the 1960s and 70s, known for albums like 'Blue' (1971) and for lyrics that mixed personal detail with sharp observation. Her 1970 song 'Big Yellow Taxi', about a parking lot paved over a paradise, was sampled for Janet Jackson's 'Got 'til It's Gone' (1997) after Jackson called Mitchell directly to ask permission, which Mitchell gave.
blurb.adult: Mitchell's songwriting, especially 'Blue' (1971), set a standard for confessional lyric-writing in rock and folk that outlasted the singer-songwriter movement she came up in. 'Big Yellow Taxi' (1970), a comparatively minor single in her own catalogue, became her best-known crossover into hip-hop and R&B production through Janet Jackson's 'Got 'til It's Gone' (1997), a cleared sample she agreed to and sang new vocals for herself.

signatureTracks.title: Big Yellow Taxi
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The source of the hook Janet Jackson sampled, and personally sang new vocals for, on 'Got 'til It's Gone'.

signatureTracks.title: Blue
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The title track of the album most often cited as her masterpiece.
